Organic revenue averaged roughly -1.4%/yr over FY2024-FY2025 per the Analysis JSON.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC; interest income not stripped, net debt company): FY2020 560.2 (continuing ops OCF 653.5 - capex 42.0 - SBC 51.3), FY2021 453.3 (615.5 - 64.1 - 98.1), FY2022 691.9 (865.4 - 94.6 - 78.9), FY2023 1220.1, FY2024 1188.8, FY2025 1167.1. FY2021-22 OCF from us-gaap:NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivitiesContinuingOperations (the CSV rows are blank). Owner-FCF CAGRs exceed reported-FCF CAGRs because SBC fell from $98M (FY2021) to $53M (FY2025); SBC is not outgrowing cash flow. scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 lands at the midpoint of the guidance raised in October (revenue +6.25%, organic about +2.75%, adjusted EBITDA ~$2.16B excluding tariff refunds), with the revenue raise not dropping through to margin because input-cost inflation and mix absorb it. The Q3 order book (orders +18% organic, IT&S book-to-bill 1.17x) carries FY2027 to 4.5% growth; thereafter organic 1-3% plus a small contribution from bolt-ons already closed or under LOI, fading to 2.5%. Underlying pre-SBC EBITDA margin recovers from 25.2% to 26.5% as Precision & Science (32.6% ex-refunds in Q3, life sciences growing low double digits) and aftermarket (~36% of sales) gain mix and IT&S pricing catches up with inflation. Ongoing M&A is value-neutral: bought at 9-10x, re-rated by IRX, with the spend and the acquired revenue both left out. The ILC Dover settlement and the tariff refunds are one-offs: the uncollected settlement sits in the equity bridge and neither is in the flows. Buybacks continue, which the flat share count does not credit.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Q3 inflection is the start of a cycle, not a lumpy quarter: long-cycle project bookings keep coming, short-to-medium cycle demand stays firm in every region, the LOI pipeline closes and re-rates to mid-teens ROIC, and life-sciences demand lifts organic growth to 4-5% for several years. FY2026 finishes at the top of the guide (+7%), fading to 3% terminal; pre-SBC underlying EBITDA margin expands to 28% as IT&S recovers the 120bp it is still down year on year and P&ST-style operational excellence is replicated, with aftermarket mix rising toward 40%. Terminal growth 3%. This case needs deal flow, organic demand and IT&S margin to all go right, which is why its weight is not raised above the bear's.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Q3 order strength proves to be one large engineered-to-order award plus pull-forward: FY2026 comes in at the low end (+5.5%), the backlog holds FY2027 at +1.5%, then industrial capex softens and revenue stalls (0%, then 1-2%). Input-cost inflation and China overcapacity keep compressing IT&S margin -- it is still down 120bp year on year excluding refunds despite positive organic growth -- and the pre-SBC underlying EBITDA margin settles at 23.5% (roughly the FY2023 level) rather than recovering. A slower deal cadence removes the growth story the premium multiple pays for; terminal growth 2%, cap 14x. No solvency question: net debt/EBITDA 1.6x and $3.9B of liquidity against $700M of notes due June 2027, so this is a re-rating bear, not a distress bear.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Ingersoll Rand is valued as a mature, moderately cyclical industrial compounder on unlevered owner FCF (EBITDA before SBC, less SBC, cash tax on EBIT after full D&A, capex and working-capital drag), discounted at a 9.75% USD WACC with net debt of $3.4B deducted, the uncollected ILC Dover settlement added back, and a flat 386.2M diluted share count. The growth path is organic-plus (guided +2% to +3.5% organic for FY2026 with a modest credit for bolt-ons in hand), not the 9-14% acquisition-inflated revenue CAGRs, and the margin driver is GAAP-underlying EBITDA rather than management's adjusted figure, so that recurring restructuring and deal costs are not treated as one-offs. Serial M&A is treated as roughly value-neutral. The market pays a low-20s multiple of guided adjusted EPS ($3.58-3.70, which adds back ~$390M/yr of acquisition amortisation), a growth premium the organic record is only beginning to support; the house valuation makes that gap explicit. Since the prior build the operating picture improved (orders, organic growth, guidance, the settlement) while the discount rate rose with Treasury yields, and the second effect is the larger.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount rate: WACC moved 9.0% -> 9.75% on a ~5.05% 10-year Treasury; that alone is -$5.80/share on the weighted value, and each 50bp is roughly $4/share on the base case. A reader who anchors on a through-cycle 4.0-4.5% risk-free rate gets a weighted value in the mid-50s

Organic growth: FY2024-25 organic revenue averaged ~-1.4%/yr; 9M-2026 is +2.7% and Q3 orders +18% organic, but the quarter includes one ~$195M award. If FY2027+ organic growth reverts to 0-1% the base case converges on the bear
IT&S margin: Q3 2026 segment adjusted EBITDA margin excluding tariff refunds down 120bp YoY (up 100bp sequentially); the base assumes recovery to 26.5% pre-SBC underlying, the bear assumes 23.5%

M&A treatment: the model neither charges acquisition cash (~$0.3-1B/yr in a normal year) nor credits acquired growth; if deals are systematically value-creating at mid-teens ROIC the model understates, if a large deal is overpaid it overstates. The ILC Dover breaches (recoveries ~18% of the purchase price) show the diligence risk is real even where it was insured
Settlement collection: $217.6M (0.56/share) in the equity bridge depends on the remaining recoveries arriving in Q4 2026 as management expects
Tariffs: gross exposure assumed offset by pricing; further IEEPA refunds are described as nominal and are unmodelled
Terminal value is roughly half of EV (47-55% across scenarios); Gordon binds in all three scenarios at a 9.75% WACC (the 16x/14x caps no longer bind)
Adjusted-vs-GAAP gap: the street values IR on adjusted EPS excluding ~$1/share of intangible amortisation; this model does not add that back beyond its tax-shield value

The cover-page date is three weeks after the balance sheet, so any October repurchases reduce the count without reducing cash; at the Q3 pace that is at most ~$100M (~$0.25/share) of flattery, the same convention as the prior build. Management's FY2026 'share count ~390.5M' is the full-year weighted average, not the current count. The 226,098 CEO PSUs approved 2026-10-27 (~$17M, FY2027-31 performance period) are unvested and expensed through SBC as they accrue. The Metrics CSV SharesOutstanding column is the diluted weighted-average series.

inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate: 10-yr UST ~5.05% (^TNX 5.07 on 2026-11-18; it has held 4.86-5.24 since mid-September) + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.1 = cost of equity ~10.55%; ~$4.7B debt at ~5.7% marginal pre-tax (4.5% after tax) on an EV of ~$35B gives ~13% debt weight; WACC 0.87 x 10.55 + 0.13 x 4.5 = 9.77%, rounded to 9.75%. CHANGED from 9.0%: the prior build's formula used a ~4.2% risk-free rate that was already stale; the formula, ERP and beta are unchanged, only the risk-free input is refreshed. At the old 9.0% the refreshed model gives bear/base/bull 40.03/57.02/66.66 and a weighted 55.18. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, China pricing and M&A execution risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), the US GAAP default: operating lease cost (~$233M liability at FY2025) is expensed inside EBITDA, so lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt. total_debt of $4,768.5M is borrowings only (term loans and senior notes).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest is immaterial (<$100M, ~$4-5M/yr of earnings); no NCI deduction and no attributable adjustment.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing: operating company, cyclical industrial -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations). UPDATE of the 2026-09-29 build after the Q3 2026 10-Q and the 2026-10-29 results release; same model, see reconciliation. WHAT CHANGED: (1) anchors -- price, net debt and cash at 2026-09-30, diluted count at 2026-10-23, and a new equity-bridge item for the uncollected ILC Dover settlement; (2) FY2026 (year 1) growth, margin and SBC% re-set to the raised/held guidance; (3) FY2027 (year 2) growth in base and bear lifted for the Q3 order book; (4) WACC 9.0% -> 9.75% on the risk-free rate. DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: growth from year 3, the EBITDA-margin path from year 2 (base to 26.5%, bull 28%, bear 23.5%), D&A, capex 1.9%, cash tax 21%/22%, working-capital capture -12%, terminal growth and cap multiples, the 25/50/25 weights, the M&A-neutral treatment and the lease/NCI treatments. What would move them: two more quarters of positive organic growth with IT&S margin ex-refunds flat or up YoY (weights toward 20/50/30 and the base margin path earlier); an FY2027 guide with organic growth above 4% (years 2-3 growth); a large acquisition above ~12x EBITDA or leverage above 3x (M&A-neutral treatment, bear weight); capex guided persistently above 2% of sales. Q3 2026 ONE-OFFS, both excluded from the flows: (a) ILC Dover representations-and-warranties settlements, gross $425.1M, $405.1M net gain in 'Other operating (income)' ($25.0M Q2, $380.1M Q3), nontaxable; $187.5M collected by 2026-09-30 and already in cash, the remainder expected in Q4 2026 and carried in the equity bridge. (b) IEEPA tariff refunds $42.6M 9M ($32.3M Q3) credited to cost of sales and included in reported adjusted EBITDA; guidance excludes the Q3 amount and the driver margin excludes all of it. Reported Q3 EBITDA $920M, net income $672M, EPS $1.73, OCF $648M and FCF $623M are therefore not run-rate; the Q3 effective tax rate of 7.4% also reflects a valuation-allowance release on foreign tax credits. EBITDA MARGIN BASIS: the driver is GAAP-underlying EBITDA before SBC, i.e. management's adjusted EBITDA (FY2026 guide held at $2.13-2.19B excluding Q3 tariff refunds, ~26.6% of the raised revenue guide) LESS the ~1.2-1.5pp of restructuring, acquisition and 'other' add-backs that recur every year for a serial acquirer. Cross-check: 9M-2026 GAAP EBITDA $1,860M - $405M settlement - $43M refunds + $50M SBC = $1,462M = 24.5% pre-SBC against adjusted ex-refunds 25.7% (gap 1.2pp), with the seasonally strongest quarter still to come; FY2025 25.7%, FY2024 25.6%. FY2025 NET INCOME of $589M and EPS $1.46 are depressed by the $229.7M goodwill + $36.1M intangible impairment in Q2 2025. INTEREST: the engine builds UNLEVERED owner FCF and deducts net debt, so interest expense ($254M FY2025; net ~$230M guided FY2026) is deliberately not in the flows; last_fcf/reported_fcf are the LEVERED FY2025 company-definition figures recorded for auditability and are not the projection base. STUB CONVENTION: fy0 stays FY2025 and year 1 is the whole of FY2026 discounted one full period, while net debt is the 2026-09-30 balance, which already holds nine months of FY2026 cash generation (largely paid out: $689M buybacks, $252M acquisitions). This is the folder's convention and the prior build's; the overlap and the unshortened discount period roughly offset. M&A: growth is organic (FY2026 guide raised to +2% to +3.5%) plus a modest credit for closed and LOI bolt-ons; acquisition cash (FY2023 $963M, FY2024 $2,959M incl. ILC Dover, FY2025 $525M, 9M-2026 $252M, plus a U.S. pump manufacturer closing 2026-10-30, price undisclosed and not in the 30 September net debt) is NOT charged and the associated revenue is NOT projected -- bolt-ons at 9-10x pre-synergy EBITDA are treated as roughly value-neutral. The ILC Dover recovery is evidence in both directions on that assumption: the deal had breaches worth ~18% of its price, and the diligence/insurance structure recovered them. D&A is ~6.8% of revenue (9M-2026) but capex only ~1.5%: most D&A is acquired-intangible amortisation, a tax shield, not a reinvestment need; the D&A path fades toward 6.0% as no new acquisitions are modelled. Interest income not stripped: net DEBT of $3.4B, the net-cash rule does not apply. The $700M senior notes due June 2027 moved to current; liquidity $3.9B, net debt / LTM adjusted EBITDA 1.6x. Working capital captured at -12% of the revenue change.

bear.growth_rationale: Y1 5.5% = bottom of the raised FY2026 guide (was 4.0%). Y2 0.5 -> 1.5: the backlog built in Q3 cushions FY2027 even if new orders soften. Stall in Y3 and later years unchanged.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 = raised FY2026 guidance midpoint 6.25% (+5.5% to +7.0%: organic +2% to +3.5%, FX ~+1%, M&A ~+2.5%); 9M-2026 ran +7.2% reported, +2.7% organic, so the guide implies Q4 at roughly +3.7%. Y2 lifted 4.0 -> 4.5 for the Q3 order book (orders +18% organic, IT&S book-to-bill 1.17x, including one ~$195M engineered-to-order award that converts over several periods). From Y3 unchanged: organic 1-3% plus ~1pp for bolt-ons in hand, fading to 2.5% terminal.
base.margin_rationale: Y1 25.2% pre-SBC underlying EBITDA: guide midpoint $2.16B excluding Q3 tariff refunds on ~$8.13B revenue = 26.6% adjusted, less ~1.4pp recurring restructuring/deal costs. Same dollars as the prior build (~$2.05B) on a higher revenue base -- management raised revenue and held EBITDA, i.e. the adjusted margin guide slipped ~25bp on input-cost inflation and mix. Q3 ex-refunds: IT&S 27.8% (down 120bp YoY, up 100bp sequentially), P&ST 32.6% (up 180bp YoY). Path from Y2 unchanged: recovery to 26.5% over five years as P&ST/aftermarket mix rises and China pricing normalises.
base.tax_rationale: Cash taxes paid / EBIT-after-full-D&A: 21.1% FY2024, 19.1% FY2025; 9M-2026 cash taxes $206.6M (9M-2025 $184.8M) track ~21% of the year-1 EBIT. GAAP ETR ~22-23% underlying (9M-2026 12.4% is distorted by the nontaxable settlement and a valuation-allowance release). 21% flat, unchanged.
base.capex_da_rationale: Capex 2.1% FY2024, 1.8% FY2025, 1.5% 9M-2026, guided ~2% of sales -> 1.9%, unchanged. D&A 6.6% FY2025 / 6.8% 9M-2026 dominated by acquired-intangible amortisation; fades to 6.0% with no new M&A modelled, unchanged.
base.sbc_rationale: 9M-2026 SBC $49.8M (9M-2025 $45.8M) annualises to ~0.81% of revenue; path moved 0.75% -> 0.80% flat in all scenarios, with the October 2026 CEO performance award accruing from FY2027.

bull.growth_rationale: Y1 7.0% = top of the raised FY2026 guide (was 6.5%). Later years unchanged.
bull.margin_rationale: Y1 trimmed 25.8% -> 25.5%: with one quarter left the top of the held EBITDA guide ($2.19B on +7% revenue = 26.75% adjusted, ~25.4% underlying) bounds the year. Later years unchanged.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35; held at the prior build's 25/50/25 after reviewing Q3 2026. Bear: the original reason (two years of negative organic revenue) has weakened -- 9M-2026 organic growth is +2.7% and Q3 orders rose 18% organic -- but one quarter carrying a single ~$195M award is not yet a trend, and IT&S margin excluding tariff refunds is still down 120bp year on year, so 25% stays. Base 50%. Bull held at 25% because it needs deal flow, sustained organic demand and IT&S margin recovery to land together. Two more quarters of positive organic growth with IT&S margin flat or better would move this to 20/50/30. No going-concern or covenant dimension (1.6x net debt/EBITDA).

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
